fixedSyntheticWitness.problem: 30 stock rows from only six independent dates can satisfy factor-level n thresholds while overall study-level date coverage comes from other factors/rows.

implications: Overall study breadth cannot substitute for factor-specific breadth when feature missingness differs by factor.
A factor with sparse source coverage can appear promotion-eligible based on clustered rows.
This is especially relevant for externally enriched or newly introduced factors whose availability is not uniform.

safeSuccessorRule.requirement: Every promotion candidate reports factor-specific train/holdout independentScanDates, years, regimes and missingness/coverage by date.
safeSuccessorRule.interpretation: Until minimum independent-date requirements are preregistered for the factor family, candidateFactor status must remain COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE rather than promotion-eligible.
safeSuccessorRule.preferredInference: Date-level effect estimates first; row count is secondary coverage only.
